significance: Stuart Clark's Thinking with Demons: The Idea of Witchcraft in Early Modern Europe (Oxford University Press, 1997) provided the comprehensive intellectual history of European demonology, arguing that demonological thought was internally coherent theological and natural-philosophical reasoning, not irrational superstition — the foundational statement of the intellectual-history approach to witch prosecution.
source_method: Clark, Thinking with Demons (Oxford University Press, 1997); catalogued and analyzed in Hutton, The Witch (2017)
